sentences.text: This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual  /Physical Mode).
2. Heard learned counsel for the Petitioner as well as learned Additional Standing Counsel for the State.
Perused the materials on record.

3. This is an application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure filed by the Petitioner for bail in connection with Tangi P.S.Case No.256 of 2021 corresponding to S.T.Case No.92 of 2022 pending in the Court of the learned 1st Additional Sessions Judge, Khurda for alleged commission of offence under Sections 365, 376(2)(n), 323, 368, 342/34 of the Indian Penal Code.
4. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the Petitioner that the Petitioner is in custody since 01.08.2021.
He further contended that in the meantime investigation has been concluded, Charge sheet has been filed.

It is also submitted before this Court that although trial has commenced,
however, the same is progressing at a slow progress.
A report was called for from the 1st Additional Sessions Judge, Khurda, who has submitted his report on 08.01.2024.

On perusal of such report, it appears that five witnesses have been // 2 // examined and the witnesses examined so far includes the father and mother of the victim and the victim herself and the case was further posted to 25.012024.
5.
Learned counsel for the Petitioner further contended that he obtained a copy of the deposition of the mother of the victim and the victim, who have been examined as P.Ws.4 & 5.
Referring to the statement of the victim, leaned counsel for the Petitioner contended that the victim has resiled from her statement and she has not supported the prosecution case.
Therefore, the learned counsel for Sanu Sidhanta Nayak vs State Of Odisha ....

the Petitioner submitted that in view of such development in a case of this nature, the entire prosecution case stands demolished on such statement of the victim.

In such view of the matter,
learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the Petitioner be enlarged on bail taking into consideration the period of detention in custody.
6. Learned Additional Standing Counsel on the other hand contended that the present case arises out of complaint case.
He further contended that the victim has resiled from her statement made before the Police in course of his examination in Court, as a result of which she has been declared hostile.
Therefore, the assertion of the learned counsel for the Petitioner does not dispute by the learned Additional standing Counsel.
Further, the fate of the trial would depend after conclusion of the trial.

7. Having heard the learned counsels for the respective parties, on careful consideration of the surrounding facts as well as the materials on record, keeping in view the development that has taken place in the meantime and taking into consideration the period of custodial detention of the Petitioner, the Petitioner be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a bail bond of Rs.40,000/- (Rupees Forty thousand) with two local solvent sureties each for the // 3 // like amount to the satisfaction of the learned court in seisin over the matter subject to the following terms and conditions:
i) The Petitioner shall not indulge in similar nature of criminal activities while on bail.
ii) shall appear before the trial Court on each and every date of posting without fail.

iii) shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence while on bail;
iv) shall not threat, influence and coerce the rest of the prosecution witnesses in any manner.
v) Violation of the condition shall entail cancellation of bail.
8. The court in seisin over the matter may impose any other condition(s) as deem fit and proper.
9. BLAPL is accordingly disposed of.
Issue urgent certified copy as per Rules.
